learn.why: Only C leaves the text alone and gives me one big friendly button, 'What is going on here?', that I can ignore. A underlines things in the middle of a paragraph and a popup covers the text and the Execute button, which feels like homework. B is a whole second tab of small text, a list, which looks like work software. C's drawer has a map and pictures, but it is still long; I would only read the first two lines. Honestly, the crisis text itself is already a wall of text for me and I would have left around there; none of these fix that.
would_turn_off: codex unlock toast (+4 new in your codex)
brief me on each new crisis
kill_criteria_hit: wall of text before the first action (crisis text plus three option cards, then drawer text)
UI looks like work software: small grey text, 'Briefing 7' list tab, small 'i' icons
popup in A covers the Execute button and the cards

answers.Q1: Donetsk oblast: never. fortress belt: later, if at all. Kramatorsk, Sloviansk: never. demilitarising: never. the Rada: later. midterms: I think US elections, later. Pokrovsk axis, Oleshky, Dnipro: never. Moscow calls it 'a basis': I do not get it. Honestly I would look up nothing right now; I want to pick a card.
answers.Q2: A: maybe, underlined words look like links so I would poke one, but the popup is huge and covers the buttons, and I would not do it twice. B: no, a side list of seven things with small text is a form, I would not open it. C: yes, one blue button and little i marks I can ignore; the drawer map is nice to look at.
answers.Q3: 'fortress belt', variant C 3/5: I can see the button, the map shows the red hatched area and the dotted circle, so I get 'the contested bit'. The text is still a lot to read. In A I found it in one hover (4/5) but the card is dense.
answers.Q4: A 2, B 4, C 4 (A: the popup hides the options and Execute; B: sits to the side, only in the way if I look at it; C: little i marks are quiet, drawer opens over the right side).
answers.Q5: I would pick 'Guide me' because I know nothing, but only if it stays short. First thing off: the underlines, then the toast and 'In your game' lines. The onboarding screen asks 'How well do you follow world news?' which is a bit of a test, I would feel judged, but the three big choices are fine and I would tap the first. The Take office button is good.
answers.Q6: Open before choosing: maybe once, if the button is bright. First read: the map, then the one-line summary. I would not read why it matters or what really happened. Missing: a plain one-line 'what each choice does to me' without Approval triple-arrow codes; the cards use words like Mobilization and Legitimacy that I cannot parse.
answers.Q7: '18 of 31 met' sounds like a collection, I like collecting a bit (like stickers), so maybe I would tap a NEW badge once. Not after the game ends, I would be gone.
answers.Q9: C: make the 'What is going on here?' button open a three-sentence card with a picture, and hide the rest behind a 'more' tap.
answers.Q10: 'As of Nov 2026' and the source count mean nothing to me and I would not read them. One wrong fact would not make me stop, I would not notice; I would just feel the game is serious. Facts flagged: []

worldmap.why: B looks like a real globe with a few numbered fires, so I know where to look and it is calmer. A has labels and pins stacked on top of each other (Iran, Pakistan, Laos card over the pins) and a huge key at the bottom with ten symbols, which looks like a chart for work. B's colours are prettier and the five fires list is easy to scan, though the right panel text gets cut off at the edge. Honest caveat: I do not know most countries on either, so what matters is that something is big and obvious to tap.
kill_criteria_hit: A: label overlaps (Iran, Pakistan, Laos card on pins; card in 2026 covers Cuba and the Pick a nation text)
A: legend of ten symbols is work-software density
B: text in the right panel is cut off at the edge in 2026
Stability colours (B) are not clear to me: what does orange mean, I would guess danger but I only guessed

answers.Q1: S1 (A): 1960, red Soviet Union and blue West, I get 'two sides'; names like Divided Berlin and A fourth atomic power mean little. S4 (B): 1960 too, I see a numbered list, five fires, which reads faster. B told me faster because of the list.
answers.Q2: Yes, 1960 has old names (Soviet Union, Belgian Congo) and sepia; 2026 is different. I do not know enough to spot mistakes. The list of leaders changed with the era which was a nice touch.
answers.Q3: Mostly readable on 1440. In S1, the Laos and Vietnam card sits on Iran and Pakistan and Trucial States overlaps. Not checked on the phone. Missing: nothing I would look for, I do not know where much is.
answers.Q4: Pin I do not get: the little purple crown with Castro's Cuba (I think a person, a leader?). The dashed and faded pins are small, I could not tell them apart from solid ones. Dotted lines versus solid red: not sure, the red arc over Europe in 2026 just looks like decoration.
answers.Q5: No, I did not notice the rim markers. I would expect tapping one to spin the globe to it.
answers.Q6: S2: card next to the pin is nicer, it pops up where I tap and has buttons Play it as a 15-minute Flashpoint, which I like. But it covers other things. S4 panel is steadier. Phone not looked at closely.
answers.Q7: B default with five fires. I would not flip the switch.
answers.Q8: Blocs colours (A) tell me who is on whose side if I know the legend; stability colours (B) are prettier but I could not say what orange means without reading. I could tell blue from red, not the orange tones from each other.
answers.Q9: A moment worth having, the year rolling and the sepia is a fun bit, and it is short. I would try 1960 just to see it, once or twice.
answers.Q10: Yes, the globe fills the screen better than a plain title. On a phone I cannot say.
answers.Q11: B. One change: make the five fires into big tappable cards with a picture, and keep labels off the map entirely until I tap.

verbatim: I do not know what a fortress belt is and I do not want homework, just give me a big button that shows me on a map and let me pick a card.
